newsitem.title: GERMANY: Meister warns against creative accounting for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Meister warns against creative accounting for EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Edgar Meister on Tuesday warned nations against being tempted to use creative accounting methods or one-off windfalls to whip its finances into shape to enter Europe's currency union.

"Already when a nation's progress in meeting entry criteria to the currency union is reviewed, the acceptance of creative accounting and one-off measures must be ruled out," Meister told a banking forum in Mainz.
He also said it was questionable whether a high measure of fiscal discipline was sustainable in the long-term.

Meister, adding his voice to a chorus of German policy makers warning that the strict entry criteria to Europe's currency union must be met honestly, also said interest income should not be used to fill budget gaps.

Meister also urged the introduction of a stability pact which would trigger sanctions against nations deviating from fiscal austerity. "A unsatisfactory quasi-automatic triggering of sanctions would lead to lax budget discipline."
In addition, Meister underscored the difference in progress reports issued by the European Monetary Institute and the European Union.

While the EMI is distinctly more critical of nations' progress, the EU takes a slightly more relaxed attitude, Meister said. He noted that the EU commission had no qualms about predicting that 12 of the total 15 European Union member nations will qualify for the currency union at the start.
"The group deliberately leaves open how lasting nations' efforts to meet convergence criteria will be," he said.
